Open Start and type your company name and your own limits in the yellow cells: the crew load you accept, the productive hours of a cleaner day, the notice for a free cancellation and the hours to confirm a visit.

Check Crews, Areas and Services: these three small tables drive the capacity and route checks. A crew is the cleaners who work together on a job, and a labour hour is one cleaner working for one hour.
Keep Clients current. The next visit, the days since the last visit and the visit check fill in by themselves, and a recurring client with no visit in 45 days turns red.
Enter every visit on Jobs. The end time, the labour hours and the phone numbers of the client, the cleaner and the team lead fill in by themselves.
Use Recurring Schedule for repeating plans: the next visit, the visits per month and the hours per month fill in, and a visit that is overdue is flagged.
Fill Crew Day Plan and Route Stops for each day. The hours free, the load and the arrival time of every stop are calculated, and an overloaded day turns red.
Write every moved visit on Reschedules and every skipped or cancelled visit on Skipped Visits with the notice and the fee, so you see the days moved and the revenue lost.
Book one-off cleans (rental turnovers, move-out cleans, post-construction cleans and deep cleans) on One-off Bookings; the days to wait show if you start quickly.
Keep Access Notes and Client Preferences complete so every crew knows how to get in, which pets to expect and which rooms to skip.
Add holidays to Holidays and prospects to Waiting List. Use Weekday Load and the Area Weekday Matrix to move clients to the days and areas with room.
Use the 14 calculators when you plan: visit duration, day plan, route time, next visit, reschedule cost, crew choice, capacity, gap filler, travel time, holiday moves, cancellation fee and more.
Read the Schedule and Routes Dashboard and Charts every week: jobs, free hours, cancellations, reschedules, new clients and the waiting list.
Know when to hire, what overtime costs and who is overloaded

Hiring pipeline with days in stage

Training records with days to expiry
One row per course taken by a cleaner with the date, the hours, the cost and the day it ends; the days to expiry and the check (valid, expires soon, expired) fill in by themselves.
Performance reviews with the overall score
One row per review with the scores for quality, punctuality, attendance and teamwork from 1 to 5; the overall score (quality counts most) and the rating fill in by themselves.
The six rules that earn a bonus, each with the level to reach (a score, a number of jobs or months) and the bonus as a share of the base pay; the bonus calculator reads the first four.
One row per piece of kit given to a cleaner with the cost and the day it came back; the days with the cleaner and whether it is returned fill in by themselves.
One row per cleaner and month with the jobs they led, the hours and the average score from 1 to 5; the hours per job fill in by themselves.
One row per shift swap with the two cleaners, the reason and who approved it; the days from today and the phones of both cleaners fill in by themselves.
One row per cleaner day with a heavy plan: the jobs and the job hours planned; the overload check against your limit and the phones of the cleaner, the team lead and the owner fill in by themselves.
The eight cleaners with the hours a week they are contracted for and their hourly rate; overtime is every hour above these.
One row per crew and month with the labour hours, the labour cost, the jobs and the revenue; the labour cost per job, the labour share and the revenue per hour fill in by themselves.
One row per van and four-week period with the crew, the kilometres and the running cost; the cost per kilometre fills in by itself.
Every person of the company and the two outside contacts with the phone and the backup person to call when they cannot be reached.
